title: DJI Air 3S live streaming: RC 2 and RC-N3 setup (2026)
description: Live stream a DJI Air 3S to YouTube, Instagram or Facebook. Choose a controller, connect DJI Fly RTMP to a phone or computer, and check the outgoing picture.
h1: How to live stream a DJI Air 3S
lead: Your DJI Air 3S can send DJI Fly’s RTMP picture to Stream My Drone on a separate phone or to Stream My Drone on a Mac or Windows PC. The controller determines which device runs DJI Fly. Follow the matching setup below, then check the receiver, framing and destination before takeoff.
summary: DJI RC 2 keeps DJI Fly on its built-in screen; a separate phone can receive and forward the feed.
RC-N3 and RC-N2 use a phone for DJI Fly. The desktop workflow keeps the receiver separate from that flight phone.
The local receiving address belongs in DJI Fly; platform credentials belong in Stream My Drone (phone or computer).
Camera recording, the controller’s live view and the outgoing RTMP broadcast have separate quality settings.
Test both the selected camera view and the platform’s viewer page before your flight.

sections.h2: Air 3S controllers: RC 2, RC-N3 and RC-N2

blocks.p: DJI’s current Air 3S FAQ lists DJI RC 2, RC-N3 and RC-N2. If you are reusing an RC-N2, update the aircraft, controller and DJI Fly before checking that they pair. Choose the workflow by the controller you actually use, rather than the name of the bundle.

blocks.note: DJI’s livestream guide limits RC 2 streaming to 720p and requires a connected microphone from DJI Fly v1.16.0. Check the available settings on your controller.

sections.h2: Air 3S with RC 2: live stream without a computer

steps.t: Install Stream My Drone on your phone
steps.d: Get the app from Google Play or the App Store. The phone receives the stream while DJI Fly stays open on the RC 2.

Join both to the same Wi-Fi with internet access. In the field, an Android phone can host the hotspot and receive the stream. Open Stream My Drone after choosing the network; on iPhone, allow local network access when requested.

steps.t: Copy the receiving address into DJI Fly
steps.d: Copy the full local receiving address shown by Stream My Drone. In DJI Fly, open GO FLY → ••• → Transmission → Live Streaming Platforms → RTMP and enter it. Use the DJI Fly RTMP guide for the menu walkthrough.

steps.t: Start the DJI Fly feed and check the preview
steps.d: Start the feed on the controller, then confirm that a moving drone picture reaches your phone. Check sound too, with any microphone required by DJI Fly connected. Keep Stream My Drone open during the test.

steps.t: Choose a destination and confirm publication
steps.d: Add a platform in Stream My Drone using its account connection where available, or its server URL and stream key. Start forwarding, then open the platform's live dashboard or viewer page. Complete any Go Live step the platform still requires.

blocks.note: The phone forwards the incoming video without re-encoding it. The preview's crop or blurred background does not turn the outgoing feed into vertical 1080×1920. Use the desktop app when you need that conversion. On iPhone, keep the app in the foreground during setup; continued background streaming depends on Picture in Picture.

sections.h2: Air 3S with RC-N3 or RC-N2: receive on a computer

blocks.p: With RC-N3 or RC-N2, keep DJI Fly open on the phone attached to the controller. Install Stream My Drone on a Mac or Windows PC, then connect the computer and flight phone to the same local network. RC 2 can use this desktop workflow too.

steps.d: Open Stream My Drone and copy the address under Connect your drone. An address such as rtmp://192.168.1.20:1935/drone is an example; use the one your app displays.

steps.t: Send DJI Fly to that address
steps.d: Enter it in DJI Fly's RTMP settings and start the feed. Allow incoming connections on your private network if the computer's firewall asks. Check the preview before adding a destination.

Choose landscape for a conventional YouTube or Facebook broadcast, or vertical output for an account using a portrait layout. Add the destination's current server URL and key, start the output, and verify the broadcast on the platform.

blocks.alt: Stream My Drone desktop showing the local DJI Fly RTMP address, platform destinations and the Start Live button.

blocks.p: Platform access belongs to your account. Receiving a drone feed in the app does not grant a stream key or publish a broadcast. For TikTok LIVE Studio, the desktop app also offers a virtual camera. Check each platform's dashboard for the current publishing step.

sections.h2: What the Air 3S camera upgrade means for your broadcast

blocks.p: DJI’s Air 3S FAQ describes its 1-inch main camera and vertical recording with both cameras. That camera upgrade does not raise the RC 2 livestream limit or guarantee a portrait RTMP picture. Judge the broadcast using what reaches your receiver.

list: Rehearse wide-angle and tele views. Select each camera in DJI Fly while the drone is on the ground. Watch the receiver for exposure, framing and the transition between views.

Check changing light. When filming a sunset or a bright skyline, watch the received picture as well as the flight screen. Adjust for an image viewers can watch immediately, rather than relying on later editing.
Test portrait delivery separately. Check the incoming dimensions, choose the desktop crop or whole-picture layout if required, and inspect the platform preview before publishing.

blocks.note: If you upgraded from Air 3, do a new ground test with Air 3S after pairing and updating. Save a fresh receiving address after any network change and check your destination credentials; the previous drone’s working broadcast is not proof of the new setup.

sections.h2: Air 3S broadcast quality and mobile data

blocks.p: The drone’s recorded file, the controller’s live view and the video sent to the receiver are separate outputs. Inspect the receiver’s input resolution before choosing output settings. Upscaling changes the size of a picture; it cannot restore detail absent from the incoming feed. Platform processing can introduce another quality change and delay.

list: Test before takeoff. Check movement, sound and the platform's viewer page while the drone is on the ground.
Budget for upload. A continuous 5 Mbps output uses about 2.25 GB per hour before network overhead. Two such destinations need about 10 Mbps combined upload and 4.5 GB per hour.
Keep the local link strong. Keep the phone or computer near the hotspot. A stable connection matters more than the network's advertised peak speed.
Watch the actual outgoing framing. On mobile, the preview layout is local. On desktop, check the selected crop or whole-picture output before publishing.

RC-N2 will not pair: confirm Air 3S is selected, update the aircraft and controller firmware and DJI Fly, and retry linking following DJI’s current instructions. Check aircraft pairing before troubleshooting the RTMP receiver.
Picture is softer than the recording: compare the receiver’s input with the DJI Fly streaming setting. A high-resolution recording mode does not remove the controller’s livestream limit.
Connection fails: copy the app's address again after a network change. Use a shared local network without guest isolation; localhost on the controller points to the controller itself.
Picture on the phone, nothing for viewers: check the destination connection, current stream key and the platform's final publishing step. Forwarding bytes alone do not confirm a public broadcast.
Stream stops after switching iPhone apps: return to Stream My Drone and check Picture in Picture. Without it, iOS can suspend the receiver.
Choppy broadcast: try one destination first, check cellular upload stability and move the receiver closer to the hotspot.
RTMP menu is missing: first confirm the aircraft connection and controller model, then check firmware and DJI Fly updates. The receiver cannot add a missing transmission menu.

blocks.p: Official model details: DJI Air 3S FAQ. RTMP procedure and controller limits: DJI Fly App Livestream Operation Guides. Firmware and manuals: DJI Air 3S downloads. Checked on October 25, 2026; available menus can change with firmware.
Compare the Air 3 streaming guide or Mini 5 Pro guide. To send the same picture to several destinations, follow the multistreaming guide.

faq.q: Can I live stream an Air 3S without a computer?
faq.a: With RC 2, use Stream My Drone on a separate phone connected to the same local network. DJI Fly runs on the controller, the phone receives its RTMP feed, and you configure the destination in Stream My Drone.

faq.q: Can I use an RC-N2 with Air 3S?
faq.a: DJI’s current Air 3S FAQ lists RC-N2 alongside RC-N3 and RC 2. Update the devices and confirm pairing first. With RC-N2, keep DJI Fly on the attached phone and use the same computer receiver workflow described for RC-N3.

faq.q: Which address goes into DJI Fly?
faq.a: The full local receiving address displayed by Stream My Drone (phone or computer). Put the platform's server URL and stream key into the receiving app's destination settings.

faq.q: Does Stream My Drone turn the video into a vertical broadcast?
faq.a: The mobile app forwards the video it receives. Its preview layout does not re-encode the outgoing picture. Stream My Drone on a computer offers vertical output conversion.

faq.q: Why can I see a preview but my audience cannot watch?
faq.a: The preview proves only that the local drone feed has arrived. Start a destination output, confirm that the platform receives it, and complete any remaining Go Live step there.

faq.q: Does Air 3S vertical recording guarantee a vertical live stream?
faq.a: Check the feed that actually reaches the receiver. Camera recording format and RTMP output are separate. The mobile app forwards incoming video, while the desktop app provides output conversion and framing controls.
